facts.fact: The page states that a company has three basic options for planning its OTT advertising strategy: publisher direct, platform direct, and programmatic.
facts.quote: A company has three basic options when planning its OTT advertising strategy.

facts.fact: The page states that OTT advertising can be bought through a guaranteed media buy or through real-time programmatic bidding.
facts.quote: Much like with original TV advertising, companies can purchase over-the-top advertising via a guaranteed media buy or real-time programmatic bidding.

facts.fact: The page states that a guaranteed media buy gives the advertiser fixed pricing and impression numbers based on audience reach and ad frequency, negotiated in advance.
facts.quote: A guaranteed media buy offers the advertiser fixed pricing and impression numbers based on the audience reach and ad frequency.

facts.fact: The page states that viewers typically cannot skip OTT ads.
facts.quote: Viewers typically can’t skip OTT ads.

facts.fact: The page states that OTT stands for “over-the-top” because the content goes over the top of traditional cable and satellite services.
facts.quote: OTT stands for “over-the-top” because this content goes over the top of the traditional cable and satellite services.

facts.fact: The page states that no set-top box is required for OTT (streaming) content.
facts.quote: No set-top box is required for OTT–or streaming–content.

facts.fact: The page states that VOD stands for video on demand, and that viewers get the content they want exactly when they want it.
facts.quote: VOD stands for video on demand, meaning viewers get the content they want, exactly when they want it.

facts.fact: The page defines OTT as the content viewers stream on apps such as Netflix, Hulu, and Amazon Prime, and defines CTV as the devices used to stream that content.
facts.quote: OTT refers to the content your audience is streaming on apps like Netflix, Hulu, and Amazon Prime. CTV, or connected TV, refers to the devices used to stream that content.

facts.fact: The page gives the article's publication date as March 18, 2022.
OTT advertising is advertising delivered through over-the-top media services such as Netflix, Hulu, or Amazon Prime.
facts.quote: OTT advertising is advertising that’s delivered through “over-the-top” media services like Netflix, Hulu, or Amazon Prime.

facts.fact: An OTT device is any device that can stream OTT content through one of the named apps or a similar platform, including smartphones, tablets, laptops, and computers.
facts.quote: An OTT device is any device that can stream OTT content via one of the apps mentioned above or a similar platform.

facts.fact: The page states that OTT ads that play mid-show are often unskippable and have higher completion rates than other advertising mediums, without giving a numeric rate.
facts.quote: These ads are often unskippable and have higher completion rates than other advertising mediums.
